description: A source-backed seven-factor Xiao relation has four nonseparating and three separating positive twists. Its normalized six-strand product passes exact sphere-action and genus-two homology checks. Three disjoint sections of square -1 are known from the literature.

sections.Surface and conventions: The double cover of the six-marked-point sphere is a closed genus-two surface. Four half twists lift to nonseparating Dehn twists; the three normalized squared twists about three-point disks lift to separating Dehn twists.
sections.Derivation: Akhmedov computes Xiao's ordered geometric monodromy from its branched-cover model. The published branch continuation is numerical, while the resulting braid decompositions and product checks are exact. Baykur-Korkmaz derive another (4,3) relation from the four-chain relation.
sections.Braid factorization: Seven printed Artin words and the corresponding normalized positive factors are recorded in fibration_lab_seeds.py. Printed factors 1 and 0 need the hyperelliptic-involution correction before lifting to the geometric separating twists. Their normalized replacements are equal upstairs, not as disk braids. The normalized product has exponent sum 40, trivial sphere outer action, and +I genus-two homology action; Birman-Hilden then gives the closed genus-two identity.
sections.Planar mapping class diagrams: The source gives labeled branch arcs and three-point circles. The normalized seven-factor seed has paired support-and-braid drawings and its own interactive Hurwitz workspace. The support pictures recover exact classes; they are not certified reconstructions of the paper's branch sketches.
sections.Standard mapping classes: The ordered factors are D, 1, R, U, infinity, L, 0: four positive half twists and three positive squared three-point twists in normalized disk representatives.
sections.Equivalences and transformations: Huang proves the Baykur-Korkmaz, Hamada, and Xiao (4,3) factorizations describe isomorphic Lefschetz fibrations. Their distinct ordered words must still retain their own conventions and provenance.
sections.Sections and multisections: Huang's Remark 4.1 gives a lift to the mapping class group of a genus-two surface with three boundary components, yielding three disjoint sections of self-intersection -1 for the equivalent (4,3) fibrations. This is source-backed section evidence; the current six-strand seed does not itself certify the boundary-framed lift.
sections.References: Akhmedov, arXiv:2609.17634, Section 8 and Appendix B; Baykur-Korkmaz, arXiv:1510.00089, Theorem 7; Huang, arXiv:2602.20451, Theorem 1.1 and Remark 4.1.
